title: HE WILL NOT PERMIT THE DESTROYER

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"When the LORD goes through the land to strike down the Egyptians, he will see
the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe and will pass over that doorway,
and he will not permit the destroyer to enter your houses and strike you down."
- Ex 12:23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"He will not permit." Those three words are worth holding on to.

The destroyer moves through Egypt that night, but it does not move freely. It
does not decide where to go. God permits or forbids, and where the blood is,
the answer is no.

This is the consistent testimony of Scripture. Evil is real and powerful, but it
is never independent. Satan had to ask permission regarding Job (Job 1:12). He
had to ask regarding Peter, and Jesus told him plainly, "I have prayed for you,
Simon, that your faith may not fail" (Luke 22:31-32).

That does not answer every hard question about suffering. Scripture does not
hand us a neat explanation for why God permits what He permits, and we should
not pretend it does. But it does tell us who is in charge. Nothing reaches a
child of God that has not passed through the hands of the Father.

Where the blood is, there is a boundary that evil cannot cross. Jesus said of
His sheep, "No one will snatch them out of my hand" (John 10:28).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you live as though evil is out of control, or under God's authority?
2. What fear would loosen its grip if you believed "He will not permit"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You set the limits. Thank You that nothing touches me without passing
through Your hands. Quiet my fears with that truth. Amen.
